rv.q: Such is the scorching talent of Sharon Duncan-Brewster and Erin Doherty that the solo set pieces are riveting – but the writing reaches its most potent intensity when they interact.
Complacency about difference has rarely been so utterly engrossing, compelling, educational or indeed, unsettling.
It may not be in the same league as its predecessors, but Closing Time is a captivating, troubling slice of modern British life that feels unsettlingly accurate, if never revelatory.

cn.t: The final installment of the Death of England trilogy earns mixed reviews, with critics finding it punchy and vital but uneven. The women-centered conclusion provokes debate but doesn't fully match the impact of earlier chapters.
